unit.title: Boundary-Safe Binary Frame Encoder
unit.purpose: Translate buffer-overflow awareness into a small, testable C component with explicit contracts, boundary reasoning, deterministic tests, and reproducible evidence.
learning_objectives: Specify memory-safety and failure-atomicity invariants before implementation.
Implement a length-delimited binary encoder without unchecked size arithmetic or partial writes on failure.
Design deterministic boundary and negative tests that distinguish functional evidence from a proof of correctness.
Produce a reproducible build, concise design record, and honest test evidence.
unit.safety_boundary: Use only a self-authored local toy component and synthetic data; no setuid binaries, external targets, network traffic, or exploitation activity.

unit_completion_requires: All requested source, test, build, design, and evidence artifacts are present.
The worker-harness-controlled validator records a passing rubric result.
The implementation and tests stay inside the stated safety boundary.
completion_policy.after_unit_completion: Record completion only for unit_kickoff_secure_binary_frame_v1. Keep the SEEDLabs course incomplete and eligible for later, separately validated expansion.
completion_policy.whole_course_completion: Not defined by this kickoff. It requires a future authoritative unit inventory, verified material availability, and independent validation of every required unit.

provenance.basis: The catalog description names C, x86 assembly, hands-on security labs, and a buffer-overflow lab example. The bounded encoder exercise and its assessment are newly authored scaffolding, not copied SEEDLabs content.
